territorial_scope.description: Applies to social network providers in Germany, and fines may be imposed for conduct not committed domestically.

evidence.quote: Die Ordnungswidrigkeit kann auch dann geahndet werden, wenn sie nicht im Inland begangen wird.

summary.short: For-profit operators of social networks (§ 1) that lack another EU member-state seat must appoint and publish a domestic service agent (§ 5). Failure is an administrative offence fined up to €500,000 (§ 4). The Bundesamt für Justiz supervises compliance (§ 4a). Enacted 1 September 2017, in force 1 October 2017.
summary.long: The Network Enforcement Act (NetzDG) applies to providers that operate platforms for profit where users share or make content publicly available (social networks). Journalistic-editorial offerings and platforms for individual communication or specific content are excluded (§ 1(1)). Unlawful content is defined by reference to listed Criminal Code offences (§ 1(3)). In this consolidated text, last amended by Art. 29 of the Act of 6 May 2024, §§ 2 to 3f are marked as removed (weggefallen). Providers without another EU member-state seat under the Digital Services Act must appoint and publicly identify a domestic service agent for court service (§ 5). Failure to do so is an administrative offence fined up to €500,000, and it may be sanctioned even if committed abroad (§ 4). The Bundesamt für Justiz is the administrative authority (§ 4). It monitors compliance and may take necessary measures, including ordering a provider to end a violation (§ 4a(1)–(2)). On request, providers must disclose measures taken, registered domestic users and complaints about unlawful content in the previous calendar year (§ 4a(3)). Transitional rules keep the Bundesamt für Justiz competent for certain pending fine proceedings (§ 6).
